questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in present perfect continuous tense form

Rama is working on this project.

options.text: Rama has been working on this project since six months.
Rama has worked on this project for six months
Rama is working on this project for six months.
Rama has been working on this project for six months.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. Rama has been working on this project for six months .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **present continuous tense**, indicating an ongoing action.
 
• To convert it into the **present perfect continuous tense**, we use the structure **"has/have been + present participle (verb+ing)"**.
 
• When the duration of the action is mentioned (e.g., "for six months"), it confirms the use of the present perfect continuous tense.

Correct sentence: *Rama has been working on this project for six months*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Perfect Continuous Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure:** has/have been + present participle (verb+ing).
 
• **Example:** She has been reading for two hours.
 
• **Usage: **Describes an action that started in the past and is still continuing or has recently stopped, often with a focus on duration.
 
 
 
• **Present Perfect Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure: **has/have + past participle.
 
• **Example: **He has completed his homework.
 
• **Usage: **Describes an action that occurred at an unspecified time in the past and is relevant to the present.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He climbed of / the steep mountain trail, / his backpack heavy / with supplies for the journey.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the preposition "**of**" after the verb "**climbed**."
 
• The correct preposition to use after "climbed" in this context is "**up**" or no preposition if the object directly follows the verb.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**He climbed up** the steep mountain trail" or "**He climbed** the steep mountain trail," ensuring grammatical correctness.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 4** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He climbed **up** the steep mountain trail, his backpack heavy with supplies for the journey."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "with supplies for the journey," **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **2: "his backpack heavy,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **3: "the steep mountain trail,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **No error** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 4.
</ul

questions.question:

questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

The table looks __proper __in the centre than in the corner.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. more proper .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence compares two positions of the table: in the centre and in the corner.
 
• When making comparisons, the word "proper" should be modified correctly to reflect the comparative degree.
 
• The word "proper" is a two-syllable adjective, so the correct comparative form is "more proper" rather than "properer" or "most proper".

Correct sentence: *The table looks **more proper** in the centre than in the corner*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Adjectives:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Adjective + "-er" or "more" + Adjective.
 
• **Example:** taller (for one-syllable words), more beautiful (for multi-syllable words).
 
• **Usage: **Used to compare differences between two objects or people.
 
 
 
• **Superlative Adjectives:**
 
 
• **Structure: **Adjective + "-est" or "most" + Adjective.
 
• **Example: **tallest (for one-syllable words), most beautiful (for multi-syllable words).
 
• **Usage: **Used to compare more than two objects or people, indicating the highest degree of the quality.

• The correct preposition to indicate reaching a specific point or place is "to".

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Along with his friend, he walked to the end of the street and came back immediately."*
